description: Custom fused batched-syrk kernel for the Newton-Schulz matrix-sign iterations in shape 11's sign-DC pipeline (ns_sign measured 16.3ms, the second-biggest shape-11 torch cost after CholeskyQR2 trsm). Each NS iteration is a symmetric product X<-1.5X-0.5X@X@X dominated by symmetric matmuls (A@A = syrk-shaped, half the FLOPs of a general GEMM since only the symmetric result triangle is needed); torch bmm computes the full product and dispatches generic GEMM. Mechanism: a fused batched CUDA kernel that computes the symmetric X@X once (syrk, upper triangle) and the cubic update in one launch per iteration keeping X resident, exploiting symmetry to halve the matmul work and cut the per-iteration launch/HBM round-trips. Targets compute-throughput / redundant-work; keep the residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback + the orthogonality-edge calibration, route guarded per shape.

Fused batched-syrk tensor-core kernel (mma.sync m16n8k8, TF32-RN) for the NS X@X: S=X@X^T upper-triangle tiles + mirror, reads X once. Correct + TF32-accurate per single step (kernel_vs_fp32 1e-4 == torch tf32) and validates 39/39, but REGRESSES: (1) first-cut kernel ~15x slower than CUTLASS s256x256 tf32gemm (ncu: 3.96ms/launch, 69% SMEM/L1-bound, 19% DRAM, 34% SM, 74% occ, 40 regs -- naive 64x64 tiles, scalar SMEM loads, no pipelining) -> ns_sign 15.4->76.9ms; (2) the 17-iter NS sign iteration DIVERGES with the kernel (orth 6.7, nbad 640/640 -> full cuSOLVER fallback) despite matching torch tf32 per-step -- gapless near-zero spectrum is the unstable fixed point of p(x)=1.5x-0.5x^3 (slope 1.5, amplifies ~1.5^17) so tiny impl differences blow up. shape11 84->346ms. Parent ns_sign=15.4ms, orth_max 0.0028-0.0051 (gate 0.0055, ~7% margin), 17 iters, per-GEMM 263-394us (parent ncu). ncu of syrk saved.

3xTF32 (hi+lo Ozaki, S=Xh@Xh^T+Xh@Xl^T+Xl@Xh^T) accumulation in the syrk kernel. Per-step ~FP32-accurate (kernel_vs_fp64=5.8e-6 FLAT, BETTER than torch allow_tf32 bmm 1.1e-4) + deterministic (0 diff/5 runs), validates 39/39, BUT the 17-iter sign iteration STILL diverges (orth 6.7, nbad 640/640 -> full fallback). Root cause is COHERENT-error amplification not precision magnitude: torch tf32/fp32/3xtf32 all converge to fp64 within 2e-4 (tolerate ~1e-4 random error), but the kernel's tiny 5.8e-6 error is DETERMINISTIC and its component along the near-zero eigenvectors (unstable fixed point of p(x)=1.5x-0.5x^3, slope 1.5) amplifies 1.5^17~985x. Also 3x slower (3 MMA passes): ns_sign 15.4->129ms, shape11 399ms. geomean 31342. Strong signal the NS sign X@X is at the batched-GEMM floor for a drop-in kernel; torch's allow_tf32 bmm is already ~1e-4 accurate + memory-bound at ~263us/GEMM.

FIXED the divergence: root cause is that the syrk computes X@X^T (=X@X only for exactly-symmetric X), but the NS iterate drifts ~3e-4 asymmetric from tf32 rounding of the cubic tail, and that asymmetry amplifies via the gapless spectrum's unstable fixed point (slope 1.5). Symmetrizing X (0.5*(X+X^T)) before the kernel fixes it -- correct + gate-safe -- and lets even 1-PASS TF32 converge (err 1.7e-4 vs fp64, == torch allow_tf32 bmm). Now nbad=0/640, orth_max 0.0031-0.0038 (gate 0.0055), 39/39, NO cuSOLVER fallback. But STILL slower: naive 64x64-tile SMEM-bound kernel (ncu t2: 3.96ms/launch, 69% SMEM-bound, 34% SM, 74% occ) + per-iter symmetrize copy -> ns_sign 15.4->137ms, shape11 203ms, geomean 29719 (better than t2/t3's 30994/31342 since no fallback, still > parent 27739). Correctness solved; kernel PERF is now the sole blocker. Open: bigger tiles + vectorized float4 loads + fuse the symmetrize into the kernel load.

128x128 register-blocked kernel (16 mma frags/warp) + FUSED symmetrize into the HBM load (symm=1). Correct + converges: nbad=0/640, orth 0.0030-0.0044, 39/39. Fused symmetrize saved the ~0.9ms/iter torch copy: ns_sign 137->116ms, shape11 182ms, geomean 29502 (best kernel-active so far, still > parent 27739). BUT ncu shows the 128x128 tile SPILLS: 255 regs/thread, Block Limit Registers=1, 12.5% occupancy, DRAM 10% / L1(local-spill) 62% / SM 17.5%, 6.2ms/launch -- WORSE than the 64x64's 4ms. Standalone: kernel core(symm0)=5.04ms vs torch.bmm 0.287ms (17x). torch's allow_tf32 bmm is the pipelined CUTLASS s256x256 floor; hand mma is 14-22x off at every tiling tried (64x64 spill-free 4ms, 128x128 spills 5-6ms). Also: torch symmetrize costs ~0.9ms (memory-bound, 3x a GEMM). ncu saved. Strong evidence NS sign X@X is at the batched-GEMM floor; symmetry saving can't overcome the pipelining gap to CUTLASS.

FINAL non-regressing state: route the syrk kernel OFF (_SIGN_DC_SYRK_KERNEL=False -> NS X@X uses torch.bmm) per the no-regression guardrail, since every kernel tiling tried is 14-28x slower per X@X than torch's CUTLASS s256x256 bmm (0.287ms). Measured geomean 27753.75 == parent 27739.4 (0.05%, within 1% noise), shape11 82023us, 39/39, nsys matches parent. The full converging syrk kernel (mma.sync m16n8k8, 1-pass + 3xTF32 hi+lo, upper-tri+mirror, fused symmetrize) + root-cause findings preserved in trials 2-5. MAPPING RESULT for the manager: the NS sign X@X is at the batched-GEMM floor -- torch's pipelined CUTLASS GEMM (0.287ms, memory-bound at the batch level, ~1e-4 accurate) is the wall; a hand mma.sync kernel is 14-28x off at every tiling (64x64 4ms spill-free, 128x128 6ms spilling 255regs/12.5%occ), and the syrk symmetry saving (half output tiles, single X read) can't overcome the CUTLASS pipelining gap. Divergence root cause (X drifts asymmetric, X@X^T != X@X) is fixed by symmetrize but the perf gap is the blocker.

Built the fused batched-syrk kernel for the NS matrix-sign X@X and MAPPED it fully. Trial-1 parent profiling (nsys+ncu, cited): ns_sign=15.4ms (stage timer), 17 deg-3 iters, each 2 batched (640,512,512) GEMMs dispatching cutlass s256x256 tf32gemm at 263-394us/GEMM, 64-87% DRAM, ~10% occupancy -> MEMORY-bound at the batch level. orth_max 0.0028-0.0051 vs gate 0.0055 (RIGHT at the gate, ~7% margin), eigr 3x cushion, nbad 0/640.

BUILT a real tensor-core syrk kernel (mma.sync m16n8k8 TF32, S=X@X^T upper-triangle tiles + mirror, reads X once; 1-pass + 3xTF32 hi+lo Ozaki + 4-term modes; fused 0.5*(X+X^T) symmetrize in the HBM load). It is CORRECT (rel vs fp64: 1-pass 8.6e-5, 3xTF32 3e-6) and validates 39/39.

TWO findings: (1) DIVERGENCE root-caused + FIXED: the syrk computes X@X^T which equals X@X only for exactly-symmetric X, but the NS iterate drifts ~3e-4 asymmetric from tf32 rounding of the cubic tail, and that asymmetry amplifies via the gapless spectrum's unstable fixed point (p'(0)=1.5, ~1.5^17). Symmetrizing X before the kernel fixes it (nbad 0/640, orth 0.003-0.0044) and lets even 1-pass TF32 converge. (2) SPEED is the blocker and maps to the batched-GEMM floor: every tiling is 14-28x slower per X@X than torch's allow_tf32 bmm (0.287ms) -- 64x64 spill-free 4ms, 128x128 spills to 255 regs/12.5% occ/6ms. torch's bmm is CUTLASS s256x256, ~1e-4 accurate (NOT nominal 1-pass), pipelined at the memory floor. The syrk symmetry saving (half output, single X read) cannot overcome the pipelining gap. Best kernel-active geomean 29502 (shape11 116ms ns_sign) vs parent 27739. Final HEAD routes the kernel OFF per the no-regression guardrail: geomean 27753.75 == parent (0.05%, within noise), 39/39; kernel+findings preserved in trials 2-5 (commits 4d25ab4d/cd70dbb1/f4ee0f85/285aa527).

CONCLUSION FOR THE MANAGER: the NS sign X@X is at/near the batched-GEMM floor for a drop-in custom kernel; torch's CUTLASS GEMM is the wall.

OPENINGS still unexplored under this objective: (a) a CUTLASS/CUTe-based syrk (CUTLASS DOES have Sm100 syrk/rank-k collectives with tcgen05 pipelining + a Syrk epilogue) instead of hand mma.sync -- that could hit CUTLASS efficiency AND the symmetry saving, the only realistic path to a win here; (b) FUSE the whole cubic 1.5X-0.5*X@X@X into ONE kernel to cut the S HBM round-trip (I only replaced X@X; the baddbmm S@X still round-trips) -- but my analysis showed n=512 is too large to keep S resident and amortize RHS re-reads, so this needs CUTLASS-grade tiling; (c) the ncu shows the parent NS GEMM is only ~10% occupancy/memory-bound -- batching the 640 matrices differently or a persistent-kernel schedule might raise occupancy, but that's torch/CUTLASS's job; (d) reduce iteration count via a degree-5/higher-order map (already a sibling lever, _SIGN_DC_NS_DEGREE) so fewer X@X regardless of kernel; (e) the symmetrize itself costs ~0.9ms/iter in torch (memory-bound) -- if a future kernel keeps X resident across the cubic, symmetrize+X@X+S@X fuse and that 0.9ms disappears. The lever remains real (ns_sign 15.4ms of half-symmetric matmuls) but needs a library-grade GEMM, not hand mma.sync.
